scope: Bounded Python standard-library JSON CLI comparing explicitly labeled synthetic product fixtures; no production or provider integration.

input_contract.fixture: Must be true; sample product IDs carry fixture- prefixes.
input_contract.schema: Map of attribute name to {type: numeric, unit?: canonical unit} or {type: categorical}.
input_contract.products: Ordered array of unique exact string IDs and attributes. Unknown attributes rejected. Absent/null values are missing.
input_contract.numeric_values: Finite number in canonical units, or {value: finite number, unit: supported unit}. Unit spellings are case-sensitive.
input_contract.preferences: Optional map: numeric {direction: min|max, weight: positive finite number}; categorical {target: string, weight: positive finite number}.
input_contract.constraints: Optional map: numeric inclusive min/max bounds accepting quantities; categorical equals string. Missing constrained attributes exclude a product.

implemented: Normalization across length, mass, volume, power, energy, time, decimal/binary storage, percentages and same-currency quantities
Side-by-side normalized values keyed by exact product IDs, missing attributes, and insufficient-data noncomparability
Weighted eligible-set min/max ranking with missing utility zero, equal known values utility one, categorical target utility, stable input-order ties
Inclusive hard constraints, explicit exclusions, empty and no-compatible statuses
Grounded selected-product advantages and disadvantages relative to other eligible products on supplied preference attributes
Optional in-process callback accepting only exact verified structured product/attribute/value claims
Strict schema, units, finite numbers, unique product IDs and duplicate JSON key validation
limitations: Synthetic fixtures only; no live catalog, fetching, installation, network, LLM provider, or business outcome evaluation.
Unit vocabulary is explicit and case-sensitive; no exchange rates, temperature offsets, compound units, locale parsing or unit aliases.
Categorical comparisons are exact strings; no semantic equivalence or inferred preferences.
Ranking scores are deterministic supplied-preference utilities, not measured business scores, probabilities, quality estimates or token measurements.
Eligible-set scaling changes when candidates change; missing utility zero may tie the known worst value.
Noncomparable means fewer than two known values in the full input set; dimensional mismatch is an input error, not an inferred conversion.
Tradeoffs compare only the first-ranked product with eligible alternatives and omit missing values; no causal or subjective claims.
Callback cannot return free-form prose; grounding validates exact facts, not arbitrary natural language.
Floating-point conversion and comparison use Python float precision; not suitable for financial settlement.
No persistence service, concurrency, streaming, large-input resource limits, or production deployment is included.

measurement.note: Parent records measured build tokens. No token counts or business scores guessed.
